An invisible mark cannot be written from the CLI by hand, but an anchored comment leaves one: dispatch comment --quote '<text of an option's line>' marks that line, and the drop of that option is the real-surface proof of finding 1.

A block holding two bullet lists cannot be made from the CLI either: an upload whose ask breaks the content rule is refused 400 INVALID_ASK_BLOCK, and a document edit that would leave it so is refused too. Only a browser's write to the live room makes it, which is what the api test does.

api's TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves refuses this pod's Postgres, whose default collation is byte order, and says so itself. It is the environment, not a failure.

discoveredComplexity: Weighing a refusal by rendering rather than by marks also answers what a comment's or a suggestion's anchor is: neither is written by the markdown, so neither is a word to lose, and an edit that drops the option they anchor in applies. The anchor dies with the text, as it does for any document edit that removes it.

The merge's refusals had to move out of the merge: settlement's restore of a decided ask's recorded wording goes through the same merge with no caller to answer a refusal, so the route weighs what an edit would delete before it builds the children (refuseLostOptionWords) and the merge itself always drops.
